rubric.why: Identifies autotrophs by their ability to make food from simple substances.
rubric.description: Autotrophs make their own food from simple inorganic substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that autotrophs make their own food, preferably noting the use of simple inorganic substances or an energy source such as sunlight.

rubric.why: Distinguishes heterotrophs by their dependence on other organisms for food.
rubric.description: Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and obtain it from other organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that heterotrophs depend on other organisms for food.

modelAnswer: Autotrophs make their own food from simple inorganic substances, using light or chemical energy.
Heterotrophs cannot make their own food and obtain it from other organisms.

items.followUp: Define fragmentation and give one example of an organism that reproduces by it.

rubric.why: Explains the essential meaning of regeneration.
rubric.description: Regeneration is the ability to replace lost body parts or develop a complete organism from a body fragment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the replacement of lost parts or the development of an organism from a fragment.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of regeneration.
rubric.description: Examples include Planaria, starfish, or a lizard regenerating its tail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example.

modelAnswer: Regeneration is the ability to replace lost body parts or, in some organisms, to develop a complete organism from a body fragment.
For example, Planaria can regenerate a complete organism from body fragments.

items.followUp: How many sets of chromosomes are present in a diploid cell and in a haploid cell?

rubric.why: Identifies the chromosome complement of a diploid cell.
rubric.description: Diploid cells have two sets of chromosomes (2n).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating two sets or 2n.

rubric.why: Identifies the chromosome complement of a haploid cell.
rubric.description: Haploid cells have one set of chromosomes (n).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating one set or n.

modelAnswer: Diploid cells contain two sets of chromosomes and are represented by 2n.
Haploid cells contain one set of chromosomes and are represented by n.

items.followUp: What is aerobic respiration? Name its main stages.

rubric.why: Defines anaerobic respiration by the breakdown of glucose without oxygen.
rubric.description: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glucose is broken down without oxygen.

rubric.why: Names the two types of anaerobic respiration.
rubric.description: Its types are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both types.

modelAnswer: Anaerobic respiration is the breakdown of glucose in the absence of oxygen.
Its two types are alcoholic fermentation and lactic acid fermentation.

items.followUp: What is the role of enzymes in lowering the energy needed for a reaction?

rubric.why: States that activation energy is the minimum energy required.
rubric.description: Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy required.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the minimum energy.

rubric.why: States that this energy is needed to start a reaction.
rubric.description: It is the energy needed to start a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the energy to starting a reaction.

modelAnswer: Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy required to start a chemical reaction.

items.followUp: What is a coenzyme? Give one example.

rubric.why: Defines a prosthetic group as a non-protein component firmly attached to an enzyme.
rubric.description: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a non-protein component tightly bound to an enzyme.

rubric.why: Gives a correct example of a prosthetic group.
rubric.description: Haem in catalase is an example of a prosthetic group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example.

modelAnswer: A prosthetic group is a non-protein component that is tightly or permanently bound to an enzyme.
Haem in catalase is an example.

items.followUp: Write any two symptoms caused by vitamin D deficiency.

rubric.why: Identifies one recognised symptom or condition associated with vitamin C deficiency.
rubric.description: One symptom is bleeding or swollen gums; vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid symptom or scurvy.

rubric.why: Identifies a second recognised symptom of vitamin C deficiency.
rubric.description: Another symptom is poor wound healing or loose teeth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one other valid symptom.

modelAnswer: Two symptoms of vitamin C deficiency are bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

items.followUp: Explain how food is moved through the oesophagus.

rubric.why: Describes the muscular action involved in peristalsis.
rubric.description: Peristalsis is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles in the alimentary canal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the wave-like muscular contractions and relaxations.

rubric.why: States the effect of peristalsis on food.
rubric.description: These movements push food along the alimentary canal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the movements push or move food forward.

modelAnswer: Peristalsis is the rhythmic contraction and relaxation of muscles in the alimentary canal.
These wave-like movements push food forward along the canal.
